subject: [PATCH] mm/memcontrol: publish null pointer before dropping css reference

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2

Author acknowledged a potential concurrency issue in drain_all_stock, where a different CPU can access percpu stock without local_lock, and agreed to restructure in v2

Author acknowledges a potential issue in refill_stock, which calls drain_stock concurrently without FLUSHING_CACHED_CHARGE set, and is considering reordering the reference drop and publishing to make intent more obvious.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Shakeel,

Thank you for the very quick review! : -D

---

I think there is a case where a different CPU can actually access the
percpu stock. drain_all_stock walks every online CPU's memcg_stock
and calls is_memcg_drain_needed, which reads the value with READ_ONCE
with no local_lock. So I think there can be a concurrent reader that
doesn't need the local lock.

---

So for drain_local_memcg_stock I agree, since FLUSHING_CACHED_CHARGE
is set, so you can't have it concurrent with drain_all_stock since it
will skip that stock. But refill_stock also calls drain_stock when
it evicts the slot but the flag isn't set, so is_memcg_drain_needed
can read it at the same time.

What do you think I should do? I think reordering makes the intent more
obvious and maybe it's just me but I did find it a bit misleading at
first that we were dropping the reference and then publishing. 

Thanks again Shakeel. Have a great day!!
Joshua

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author clarified that their original patch was based on an assumption about their own previous code, which actually already addressed the issue by switching the order of reference drop and publishing.
reviews.raw_body:
Oh and just for clarification, my page_counter_stock series actually
gets rid of this codepath and switches the order when moving it anyways.
I just thought I would pull this out early and send it as a fix to see
if it would be worth the effort!

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Reviewer Shakeel Butt questioned the existence of a race condition in the patch, citing a scenario where CPU 1 and CPU 2 can access the same memcg simultaneously due to PREEMPT_RT's behavior with per-CPU spinlocks. He used AI reasoning to conclude that this is indeed a racy access on PREEMPT_RT.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes but this patch has fixes and might get backported, so we need to be use it
is fixing an issue which is real.

Let's try to reason how the race can happen between is_memcg_drain_needed and
drain_stock:

CPU 1						CPU 2

drain_stock
  WRITE_ONCE(stock->nr_pages[i], 0);		is_memcg_drain_needed
  css_put(&old->css);
  /* assume full grace period */
  						  rcu_read_lock()
  						  memcg = READ_ONCE(stock->cached[i]);
  						  if(READ_ONCE(stock->nr_pages[i])
  							mem_cgroup_is_descendant(memcg);

  WRITE_ONCE(stock->cached[i], NULL);


Do you think there is possible race condition in above? I couldn't see.

However I ran this through AI and it has convinced me that on PREEMPT_RT, this
is indeed racy access.

AI reasoning:
-------------

How it breaks on PREEMPT_RT

On RT, local_trylock() takes a per-CPU spinlock_t (an rtmutex). That is
rcu_read_lock() plus migrate_disable(), but the task can still be preempted
inside it.

1. CPU A, refill_stock(X): there is no free slot, so it calls drain_stock(i) on
   old. It sets nr_pages[i] = 0, then css_put(old) drops the last reference and
   queues the release work on CPU A.
2. The refill task is preempted (by a tick or a threaded IRQ) before it clears
   cached[i]. CPU A's kworker runs css_release_work_fn(), which calls call_rcu(),
   and grace period G starts. G will wait for the refill task, because that task is
   inside an RCU reader.
3. CPU B, drain_all_stock() \u2192 is_memcg_drain_needed(): B has already passed a
   quiescent state for G. It enters rcu_read_lock() and loads cached[i] == old. G
   does not wait for this reader, because it started after G did.
4. B is preempted right after that load (RT readers can be preempted).
5. A resumes. It clears cached[i], puts X in slot i with a non-zero nr_pages[i],
   and unlocks. G ends, and old is freed.
6. B resumes. It reads X's non-zero count and calls
   mem_cgroup_is_descendant(old, root). That reads old->css.cgroup from freed
   memory.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged the feedback as a potential PREEMPT_RT race condition and agreed to restructure the patch in v2, including a new commit message that explains the issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for taking a look. I think this is the race condition that Sashiko
brought up in the original series that I had.

I will go ahead and send a v2 with a new commit message that explains
this PREEMPT_RT race condition so that it is more obvious where it can
actually race in a kernel. Thanks!

Joshua

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch fixes a rare issue where a memory cgroup (memcg) could be freed while still being referenced by the memcg's stock, leading to a null pointer dereference. The fix involves publishing a NULL pointer before dropping the reference to the cgroup, ensuring that any readers waiting for the RCU grace period are properly notified and can safely access the now-freed memory. This change is based on a report from Sashiko and fixes an issue introduced in a previous patch series by Joshua Hahn.
